stem: You are taking a history course with Professor Okafor. For the final project, the professor put you in a group of four students who must give a presentation together in two weeks. Last week your group held two planning meetings, but one member, Lucas, did not come to either of them and has not answered any messages. Without his part of the research, the group cannot finish the slides on time. You want to ask the professor for advice.
task: Write an email to Professor Okafor. In your email, do the following:
bullets: Explain the problem your group is having.
Describe what the group has already tried.
Ask the professor for advice or suggest a possible solution.
explanation:
Dear Professor Okafor,
I am writing about my group's final project for your history course. One of our four members, Lucas, has not been able to take part so far, and we are worried about finishing the presentation on time.
Last week we held two planning meetings, and Lucas did not attend either one. We have also sent him several messages and emails, but he has not replied. Because his section covers the economic background, the rest of the slides depend on it.
Could you advise us on how to handle this? One possible solution would be for the three of us to divide his section and present it ourselves, with each person's contribution noted on the final slide. If you prefer a different approach, we would be happy to follow it.
Thank you for your time.
Best regards,
Sam
points: States the problem clearly in the first paragraph without blaming Lucas in a rude way.
Gives concrete details of what the group has tried (two meetings, several messages).
Makes a specific, reasonable suggestion and still leaves the decision to the professor.
Uses a polite, formal tone suitable for a professor, with a clear greeting and closing.

stem: You rent a small apartment near the university. Three days ago the heating system in your apartment stopped working, and the nights have become very cold. You called the landlord, Ms. Rivera, twice, but both times you reached her voicemail and she has not called back. You have an important exam next week and need to study at home in the evenings. You decide to send her an email instead.
task: Write an email to your landlord, Ms. Rivera. In your email, do the following:
bullets: Describe the problem with the heating.
Explain how the problem is affecting you.
Give details of when you are available for a repair visit.
explanation:
Dear Ms. Rivera,
I am writing because the heating in my apartment, unit 4B, stopped working three days ago. I tried to call you twice, but I reached your voicemail, so I thought an email might be easier.
The radiators are completely cold, even when the thermostat is set to the highest temperature. At night the apartment becomes very cold, and it is difficult to sleep. I also have an important exam next week, and I need to study at home in the evenings, which is hard in these conditions.
I would be grateful if a repair person could come as soon as possible. I am at home every day after 3 p.m., and I am free all day on Saturday. If another time is better, please let me know and I will try to arrange it.
Thank you for your help.
Best regards,
Sam
points: Identifies the apartment and the problem precisely (what stopped working and when).
Explains the effect on daily life and studying without sounding angry.
Gives clear, specific times when a repair visit is possible.
Stays polite and formal while making the urgency clear.

stem: You work part-time at a café on campus. Your manager, Mr. Chen, makes the staff schedule two weeks in advance. Yesterday the university published the final exam timetable, and you found out that two of your exams are on mornings when you are scheduled to work. One of them is on a Tuesday and the other on the following Thursday. You do not want to leave your coworkers short of staff.
task: Write an email to your manager, Mr. Chen. In your email, do the following:
bullets: Explain the schedule conflict.
Ask for a change to your schedule.
Suggest a way to cover your shifts.
explanation:
Dear Mr. Chen,
I hope you are well. Yesterday the university released the final exam timetable, and I have found that two of my exams fall on mornings when I am scheduled to work: Tuesday the 9th and Thursday the 11th.
I am sorry for the short notice. Would it be possible to move me off those two morning shifts? I understand that exam weeks are busy at the café, so I do not want to leave the team short.
I would be happy to work extra afternoon or evening shifts that week to make up the hours. I have also spoken with Amara, who said she could take the Tuesday morning if you agree. I can check with other coworkers about Thursday as well.
Thank you for considering my request.
Best regards,
Sam
points: Explains the conflict with exact days so the manager can act on it.
Asks for the change politely and acknowledges the inconvenience.
Offers a practical solution, such as swapping shifts or working extra hours.
Keeps a respectful, professional tone suitable for an employer.

stem: Last week you ordered a desk lamp from an online home goods store called Brightway. The lamp arrived yesterday, but the glass shade was cracked and the switch did not work when you plugged it in. You still need a lamp for your desk because you often study late at night. The store's website says customers can contact the customer service team by email about damaged items.
task: Write an email to Brightway customer service. In your email, do the following:
bullets: Describe what was wrong with the item you received.
Explain why you need the problem solved quickly.
Ask for a specific solution.
explanation:
Dear Customer Service Team,
I am writing about my recent order, number 58213, for a white desk lamp. The package arrived yesterday, but unfortunately the lamp was damaged. The glass shade has a long crack down one side, and when I plugged the lamp in, the switch did not turn it on.
I bought this lamp because I often study late at night, and my room does not have enough light without it. For this reason, I would like the problem to be solved as quickly as possible.
Could you please send me a replacement lamp by express delivery? I can return the damaged one with a prepaid label if you send me one. If a replacement is not available, I would prefer a full refund.
I have attached two photos of the damage. Thank you for your help.
Best regards,
Sam
points: Gives the order details and describes the damage precisely.
Explains briefly why the item matters, which supports the request for speed.
Requests a clear solution (a replacement or a refund) and offers to return the item.
Is polite and businesslike rather than angry.

stem: You are a member of the campus photography club. The club meets every Wednesday evening, and members borrow cameras and lighting equipment from a storage room in the art building. For the last two Wednesdays, the storage room was locked when members arrived, and no one had the key. Several new members left early because they could not use any equipment. You want to tell the club president, Hamza, about this.
task: Write an email to the club president. In your email, do the following:
bullets: Describe what happened at the last two meetings.
Explain why this is a problem for the club.
Suggest a solution.
explanation:
Hi Hamza,
I wanted to let you know about a problem at our last two Wednesday meetings. Both times, the equipment room in the art building was locked when we arrived, and nobody there had a key. We waited about twenty minutes, but in the end we could not borrow any cameras or lights.
This is a real problem for the club, especially for new members. Several of them do not own cameras yet, so they left early. I am worried that some of them may stop coming if this keeps happening.
One idea is to give a second key to another officer, such as the treasurer, so that someone can always open the room. We could also ask the art building staff to unlock it at 6 p.m. on Wednesdays.
Thanks for looking into this.
Best regards,
Sam
points: Describes the specific events at the two meetings.
Explains the effect on the club, especially on new members.
Offers one or two practical solutions.
Uses a friendly but clear tone suitable for a fellow student who leads the club.

stem: You are taking an introductory biology course. Last Monday you were sick and missed the lecture, which covered cell division, a topic that will be on next week's quiz. The professor does not post lecture notes online. Your classmate Priya sits next to you in class and always takes very detailed notes. You also have a lab report due on Friday, and you know Priya is still working on hers.
task: Write an email to your classmate Priya. In your email, do the following:
bullets: Explain why you missed the lecture.
Ask for her help with the notes.
Offer something in return.
explanation:
Hi Priya,
I hope your week is going well! I wasn't in biology on Monday because I had a bad fever and spent most of the day in bed. I'm feeling much better now, but I'm a little worried because I missed the whole lecture on cell division.
Since that topic will be on next week's quiz, I was wondering if I could borrow your notes from Monday. I know you take really detailed notes. You could send me photos of the pages, or I could copy them quickly after class on Thursday.
In return, I'd be happy to help with the lab report due Friday. I've already finished the data analysis section, so we could go through the graphs together at the library if that would be useful.
Thanks so much!
Best regards,
Sam
points: Gives a brief, clear reason for missing the class.
Makes a specific request and suggests easy ways to share the notes.
Offers a fair, concrete favor in return.
Uses a friendly, informal tone with contractions, suitable for a classmate.

stem: You live on Maple Street, a quiet residential road near a public park. For about two weeks, two of the streetlights on your block have not been working, so the sidewalk is very dark in the evening. Many people, including children and older residents, walk to the park after sunset. The city's Public Works Office has an email address for reporting problems with streets and lighting.
task: Write an email to the city's Public Works Office. In your email, do the following:
bullets: Describe the problem and where it is.
Explain why the problem is important to fix.
Ask what the office will do and when.
explanation:
Dear Public Works Office,
I am writing to report two broken streetlights on Maple Street. They are on the block between Elm Avenue and the entrance to Riverside Park, one in front of number 42 and the other near the bus stop. Neither light has worked for about two weeks.
This section of the street is now very dark after sunset. Many residents, including children and older people, walk to the park in the evening, and it is difficult to see the uneven parts of the sidewalk. I am concerned that someone could fall or feel unsafe.
Could you please let me know whether a repair has been scheduled and approximately when the work will be done? If you need more information, I would be glad to help.
Thank you for your attention to this matter.
Best regards,
Sam
points: Gives the exact location so the office can find the problem easily.
Explains the safety concern with specific details about who is affected.
Asks a clear question about action and timing.
Uses a polite, formal tone appropriate for a government office.

stem: Two weeks ago you borrowed three books from the university library. You returned all of them on time by putting them in the book drop outside the main entrance. However, yesterday you received an email saying that one of the books, a guide to statistics, is overdue and that you owe a fine of eight dollars. You are sure you returned it with the others on the same evening.
task: Write an email to the library's circulation desk. In your email, do the following:
bullets: Explain what you did with the books.
Describe the problem with your account.
Ask the library to take a specific action.
explanation:
Dear Circulation Desk Staff,
I am writing about a fine on my library account. Two weeks ago I borrowed three books, and I returned all of them on the evening of October 12 by putting them in the book drop outside the main entrance. This was two days before the due date.
Yesterday, however, I received an email saying that one of the books, Practical Statistics for Beginners, is overdue and that I owe eight dollars. The other two books were checked in correctly, so I believe this one may have been missed or placed on the wrong shelf.
Could you please check the shelves and the return area for this book? If you find it, I would appreciate it if you could remove the fine from my account. My student ID number is 2047731.
Thank you for your help.
Best regards,
Sam
points: Gives a clear account of when and how the books were returned.
Describes the problem with specific details (which book, the amount of the fine).
Suggests a possible explanation politely instead of accusing the staff.
Asks for a concrete action and provides information needed to find the account.

stem: You are a graduate student, and your poster about water quality in local rivers was accepted for a regional environmental science conference. The organizers scheduled your poster session for Friday at 9 a.m. Yesterday the airline changed your flight, and you will now arrive on Friday at around noon. The conference continues until Saturday afternoon. You want to contact the conference organizers, led by Dr. Mendes.
task: Write an email to the conference organizers. In your email, do the following:
bullets: Explain your situation.
Ask for a change to your poster session.
Give details of when you will be available.
explanation:
Dear Dr. Mendes,
Thank you again for accepting my poster, "Seasonal Changes in Water Quality in Local Rivers," for this year's conference. Unfortunately, I am writing because of an unexpected travel problem.
Yesterday my airline changed my flight, and I will now arrive in the city at around noon on Friday. As a result, I will not be able to present at my scheduled poster session at 9 a.m. that day.
Would it be possible to move my poster to a later session? I will be available any time from 2 p.m. on Friday until the end of the conference on Saturday afternoon. If no other session has space, I could also hang my poster on Friday afternoon and stand by it during a break.
I apologize for the inconvenience and appreciate your help.
Best regards,
Sam
points: Explains the travel change clearly and early in the email.
Makes a polite, specific request for a different session.
Gives exact availability so the organizers can easily find a new slot.
Offers a flexible alternative and keeps a formal, professional tone.

stem: You are doing a summer internship at a marketing company. Your supervisor is Ms. Adeyemi. Your university has just announced that the graduation ceremony will take place on a Thursday next month, and your family is traveling from another city to attend. You will need to take that Thursday and the following Friday off. You are currently helping your team prepare a report that is due at the end of that month.
task: Write an email to your internship supervisor. In your email, do the following:
bullets: Explain why you need time off.
Ask for permission to take the days off.
Explain how you will make sure your work is done.
explanation:
Dear Ms. Adeyemi,
I hope you are having a good week. I am writing to ask about taking two days off next month. My university has just announced that the graduation ceremony will be held on Thursday the 18th, and my family is traveling from another city to attend.
Would it be possible for me to take Thursday the 18th and Friday the 19th off? I wanted to ask well in advance so that the team can plan around my absence.
I know the client report is due at the end of the month. To make sure it stays on schedule, I plan to finish my section on social media data by Tuesday the 16th. I could also stay a little later on the days before I leave if that would help.
Thank you for considering my request.
Best regards,
Sam
points: Gives the reason and the exact dates clearly.
Asks for permission politely rather than simply announcing the absence.
Shows responsibility with a specific plan for finishing the work.
Uses a professional, respectful tone appropriate for a workplace supervisor.

stem: You are taking a chemistry course with Professor Lindqvist, and a research paper based on your own lab experiment is due next Monday. Last week the machine you needed to measure your samples broke down, and the lab technician says it will not be repaired until Wednesday. Without these measurements, you cannot complete the results section of your paper. You have already finished the introduction and the methods section.
task: Write an email to Professor Lindqvist. In your email, do the following:
bullets: Explain what happened in the lab.
Describe the progress you have made so far.
Ask for an extension and suggest a new deadline.
explanation:
Dear Professor Lindqvist,
I am writing about the research paper that is due next Monday. Last week the spectrometer that I need to measure my samples broke down. The lab technician told me it will not be repaired until Wednesday, so I have not been able to collect the data for my results section.
I have already finished the introduction and the methods section, and my samples are prepared and stored correctly. As soon as the machine is working again, I can complete the measurements in one afternoon.
Would it be possible to have a short extension? I would suggest Friday of next week as a new deadline, which would give me enough time to analyze the data and write the discussion carefully. I am also happy to send you my finished sections now.
Thank you for your understanding.
Best regards,
Sam
points: Explains the cause of the delay clearly and shows it was outside the student's control.
Shows progress with specific details, which makes the request more convincing.
Requests a specific, reasonable new deadline instead of an open-ended extension.
Uses a polite, formal tone suitable for a professor.

stem: You rent an apartment from Mr. Kowalski, and your one-year lease ends in August. This summer you have been offered a three-month research position in another city, from June to August. You would like to keep your apartment for next year, but you do not want to pay rent for an empty apartment while you are away. A friend of yours, Mateo, is looking for a place to stay for the summer.
task: Write an email to your landlord, Mr. Kowalski. In your email, do the following:
bullets: Explain your plans for the summer.
Ask whether you are allowed to sublet the apartment.
Give details about the person who would stay there.
explanation:
Dear Mr. Kowalski,
I hope you are doing well. I am writing to ask about my apartment for this summer. I have been offered a research position in another city from June 1 to August 31, and I plan to accept it. However, I would very much like to renew my lease and stay in the apartment next year.
Would you allow me to sublet the apartment while I am away? I would continue to be responsible for the rent and for any damage, and I would make sure everything is in good condition when I return.
The person who would stay there is my friend Mateo, a graduate student in engineering. He is quiet and tidy, does not smoke, and has no pets. He would be happy to meet you before June if you would like.
Thank you for considering this.
Best regards,
Sam
points: Explains the summer plans and the dates clearly.
Asks permission directly and politely, and shows the tenant will stay responsible.
Gives reassuring, relevant details about the subtenant.
Uses a respectful, formal tone appropriate for a landlord.

stem: You are a member of the campus recreation center and have signed up for an evening yoga class that meets on Tuesdays and Thursdays. In the past three weeks, the class has been canceled four times, and each time the notice was posted on the website less than an hour before it was supposed to start. You paid a fee for the whole semester. You want to contact the center's program manager, Ms. Haddad.
task: Write an email to the program manager. In your email, do the following:
bullets: Describe what has happened with the class.
Explain how this has affected you.
Suggest a way to improve the situation.
explanation:
Dear Ms. Haddad,
I am writing about the evening yoga class on Tuesdays and Thursdays, which I signed up for this semester. Over the past three weeks, the class has been canceled four times. Each time, the notice appeared on the website less than an hour before the start.
These late cancellations have been frustrating. Twice I had already walked to the center from the library when I found out, and I had planned my study schedule around the class. Since I paid for the whole semester, I feel I am missing much of what I paid for.
I would like to suggest two changes. First, could the center send a text or email to students as soon as a class is canceled? Second, it would be helpful to have a substitute instructor or a make-up session when the regular teacher cannot come.
Thank you for your attention.
Best regards,
Sam
points: Summarizes the problem with clear numbers and timing.
Explains the personal effect without exaggerating or sounding rude.
Offers constructive, specific suggestions rather than only complaining.
Keeps a polite, formal tone suitable for a program manager.

stem: You and your friend Kwame planned a weekend trip to a lake about two hours away. You were going to drive there on Saturday morning in your car and come back on Sunday evening. Yesterday a mechanic told you that your car needs a repair that will take several days. You still want to go on the trip, and you know there is a bus that goes near the lake.
task: Write an email to your friend Kwame. In your email, do the following:
bullets: Tell him what happened to your car.
Explain how this affects your plans.
Suggest a different way to make the trip.
explanation:
Hi Kwame,
I've got some bad news about our lake trip. I took my car to the garage yesterday because the brakes were making a strange noise, and the mechanic said it needs a repair that will take at least four days. So the car definitely won't be ready by Saturday.
That means we can't drive there the way we planned, and we'd also need to rethink how to carry the tent and the cooler.
I still really want to go, though! I checked online, and there's a bus that leaves the central station at 8:30 on Saturday morning and stops about a mile from the lake. Tickets are only twelve dollars each. We'd just need to pack lighter. What do you think? If you'd rather wait, we could also go the following weekend.
Best regards,
Sam
points: Explains the car problem briefly and clearly.
Shows how the change affects the original plan.
Suggests a practical alternative with useful details (time, price).
Uses a relaxed, friendly tone with contractions, suitable for a friend.

stem: For your economics course, you ordered a textbook from the campus bookstore's website. The course list says students need the fifth edition, but the book you received last week is the fourth edition. The professor has already assigned homework from chapter twelve, which does not exist in the older edition. The first homework set is due in five days, and you have not been able to start it.
task: Write an email to the bookstore's customer service department. In your email, do the following:
bullets: Explain what you ordered and what you received.
Describe the problem this has caused.
Ask for a specific solution.
explanation:
Dear Customer Service Team,
I am writing about my online order number 71904. I ordered the fifth edition of Principles of Economics for my course, as listed on the required reading page. However, the book I received last week is the fourth edition.
This has caused a problem with my coursework. My professor has assigned homework from chapter twelve, which does not exist in the older edition. The first assignment is due in five days, and I have not been able to start it.
Could you please exchange the book for the correct edition as soon as possible? I can bring the fourth edition to the store tomorrow, so it would be ideal if I could pick up the fifth edition at the same time. If it is out of stock, please let me know when it will arrive.
Thank you for your help.
Best regards,
Sam
points: Clearly contrasts what was ordered with what was received.
Explains why the mistake matters, with the deadline as a detail.
Asks for a clear exchange and suggests how it could happen quickly.
Uses a polite, businesslike tone.

stem: You volunteer at the city's natural history museum, where you guide school groups on Saturdays. The volunteer coordinator, Mr. Abara, has announced a required training session next Saturday morning about the museum's new dinosaur exhibit. However, you will be taking a university entrance exam that morning, which you registered for months ago. You want to stay in the volunteer program and lead tours of the new exhibit.
task: Write an email to the volunteer coordinator. In your email, do the following:
bullets: Explain why you cannot attend the training.
Show that you still want to take part in the program.
Suggest another way for you to receive the training.
explanation:
Dear Mr. Abara,
Thank you for organizing the training session on the new dinosaur exhibit next Saturday. Unfortunately, I will not be able to attend, because I am taking a university entrance exam that morning. I registered for the exam several months ago, and it cannot be moved.
I am very sorry to miss it, because I really enjoy guiding school groups and I am excited about the new exhibit. I would love to lead tours of it once it opens.
Would it be possible for me to catch up in another way? For example, I could join a later session if there is one, or I could come in on a weekday afternoon and follow an experienced guide through the exhibit. If there are any training materials or slides, I would also be happy to study them at home.
Thank you for understanding.
Best regards,
Sam
points: Gives a clear, acceptable reason for missing the required session.
Shows enthusiasm and commitment to the volunteer role.
Suggests one or more realistic alternatives for catching up.
Uses a polite, appreciative tone suitable for a coordinator.

stem: You live in a university residence hall. For the past ten days, the wireless internet on your floor has been extremely slow in the evenings and often disconnects completely. Many students on your floor have the same problem. You take two online courses this semester, and last night you were disconnected in the middle of an online quiz. You decide to write to the Student Housing Office.
task: Write an email to the Student Housing Office. In your email, do the following:
bullets: Describe the problem with the internet.
Explain how it is affecting your studies.
Ask the office to take action.
explanation:
Dear Student Housing Office,
I live on the third floor of Hillside Hall, room 312, and I am writing about the wireless internet on our floor. For about ten days, the connection has been very slow in the evenings, especially between 7 and 11 p.m., and it often disconnects completely. Several other students on my floor have noticed the same problem.
This is seriously affecting my studies. I am taking two online courses this semester, and most of the lectures and quizzes take place in the evening. Last night I was disconnected in the middle of an online quiz and lost several answers.
Could you please ask the technical team to check the network equipment on our floor? In the meantime, it would help to know whether there is a study area in the building with a more reliable connection.
Thank you for your help.
Best regards,
Sam
points: Gives precise information about the location and the timing of the problem.
Mentions that other students are affected, which shows it is not an isolated issue.
Explains the academic impact with a concrete example.
Makes a clear, polite request and asks about a temporary solution.

stem: You are a second-year student studying psychology. To graduate on time, you must take a research methods course this coming semester. When you tried to register online this morning, the system said the course was full, and the waiting list already has fifteen names. Your academic advisor, Dr. Nakamura, helps students plan their courses and can sometimes give special permission to join a class.
task: Write an email to your academic advisor, Dr. Nakamura. In your email, do the following:
bullets: Explain the problem with registration.
Explain why the course is important for you.
Ask for help and suggest possible options.
explanation:
Dear Dr. Nakamura,
I hope you are well. I am writing because I tried to register this morning for Research Methods in Psychology, but the system showed that the course is full. The waiting list already has fifteen students on it.
This course is very important for me, because it is required for my major and it is a prerequisite for two courses I plan to take next year. If I cannot take it this semester, I am worried that I will not be able to graduate on time.
Could you help me find a solution? One option might be special permission to join one of the existing sections. Alternatively, if a new section is opened, I would be happy to take it at any time, including early mornings or evenings. I could also meet you during your office hours to discuss my plan.
Thank you very much.
Best regards,
Sam
points: Describes the registration problem with clear facts.
Explains the importance of the course for graduation and future courses.
Asks politely for help and suggests realistic options.
Uses a formal tone appropriate for a faculty advisor.

stem: You are a member of the university debate club, which meets every Monday at 4 p.m. This semester, many members are taking science courses with labs that run until 5 p.m. on Mondays, so attendance at meetings has dropped from about twenty students to eight. The club has an important regional competition in two months. You want to write to the club leader, Sofia, about the meeting time.
task: Write an email to the club leader. In your email, do the following:
bullets: Describe the problem with attendance.
Explain why it matters now.
Suggest a new meeting time and a way to choose it.
explanation:
Hi Sofia,
I wanted to share something I've noticed about our Monday meetings. This semester, attendance has dropped from around twenty people to only eight. After talking to a few members, I found out that many of them have science labs on Mondays that don't finish until 5 p.m., so they simply can't make it.
This is worrying because the regional competition is only two months away. If half the team misses our practice debates, it'll be hard to prepare everyone properly and choose strong teams.
Would you consider moving our meetings? Wednesday at 6 p.m. might work, since the classrooms in the humanities building are free then. To make sure it suits most people, we could send a quick online poll with two or three possible times and pick the most popular one.
Let me know what you think!
Best regards,
Sam
points: Describes the drop in attendance with numbers and a reason.
Connects the problem to the upcoming competition.
Suggests a specific new time and a fair way to decide.
Uses a friendly, cooperative tone suitable for a student leader.

stem: You are in a study group with three classmates for your statistics course. The group meets every Thursday evening, and this week it is your turn to host the meeting in your apartment. However, the building's management has just told residents that water will be shut off on Thursday evening for pipe repairs. You want the group to meet anyway, because there is a test on Monday. You email your classmate Yuki, who organizes the group.
task: Write an email to your classmate Yuki. In your email, do the following:
bullets: Explain why you cannot host the meeting.
Suggest another place to meet.
Give details of what you can bring or prepare.
explanation:
Hi Yuki,
I'm afraid I can't host our study group this Thursday after all. My building just announced that the water will be shut off on Thursday evening for pipe repairs, so there won't be any water in my apartment for coffee or even the bathroom!
I still think we should meet, though, especially with the statistics test on Monday. How about booking one of the group study rooms on the second floor of the library? They're free to reserve online, and they have big whiteboards, which would be perfect for working through problems together.
To make up for not hosting, I'll bring snacks for everyone. I can also print copies of last year's practice test and prepare a short summary sheet of the formulas from chapters six and seven.
Let me know if that works for everyone.
Best regards,
Sam
points: Explains the reason for the change briefly and clearly.
Suggests a convenient alternative location with a reason it works well.
Offers specific, useful contributions to the meeting.
Uses a friendly, informal tone with contractions, suitable for a classmate.

stem: Last month you booked a table for eight people at an Italian restaurant called Casa Lena to celebrate your sister's birthday. You received a confirmation email at the time. However, when your group arrived on Saturday evening, the staff said they had no record of your booking, and you waited almost an hour for a table. You want to write to the restaurant's manager, Mr. Romano.
task: Write an email to the restaurant manager. In your email, do the following:
bullets: Describe what happened when you arrived.
Explain how this affected your celebration.
Ask the restaurant to do something about it.
explanation:
Dear Mr. Romano,
I am writing about my visit to Casa Lena last Saturday evening. I had booked a table for eight people at 7 p.m. to celebrate my sister's birthday, and I received a confirmation email when I made the reservation. However, when we arrived, the staff told us there was no record of our booking.
We ended up waiting almost an hour before a table was free. My sister's birthday dinner started very late, two older relatives became quite tired, and the evening was much more stressful than we had hoped.
I have attached the confirmation email so that you can check what went wrong. I would appreciate an explanation, and I would also like to ask whether the restaurant could offer a partial refund or a discount on a future visit.
Thank you for taking the time to read this.
Best regards,
Sam
points: Gives clear facts about the booking and what happened on arrival.
Explains the effect on the celebration in a calm, specific way.
Supports the complaint with evidence (the confirmation email).
Makes a reasonable request and keeps a polite, formal tone.

stem: You are taking a sociology course, and quizzes are graded by the teaching assistant, Olga. Yesterday you got your third quiz back with a score of 14 out of 20. When you added up the points written next to each question, however, the total came to 17. You also think one of your short answers may have been marked wrong by mistake, because it matches the definition in the textbook.
task: Write an email to the teaching assistant. In your email, do the following:
bullets: Explain what you noticed about your quiz score.
Describe the second problem you found.
Ask her to review the quiz and suggest how.
explanation:
Dear Olga,
I hope you are having a good week. I am writing about my score on Quiz 3, which I received back in class yesterday. The score at the top of the page is 14 out of 20, but when I added up the points next to each question, the total came to 17. I think there may have been a small error in the addition.
I also have a question about question 6. My answer was marked incorrect, but it seems to match the definition of "social mobility" on page 84 of the textbook.
Would you be willing to look at the quiz again? I could bring it to your office hours on Wednesday, or I could leave a copy in your mailbox in the department office, whichever is easier for you.
Thank you very much for your time.
Best regards,
Sam
points: Explains the scoring error with exact numbers.
Raises the second issue politely and supports it with evidence from the textbook.
Asks for a review and offers convenient ways to share the quiz.
Uses a respectful tone that does not accuse the teaching assistant.

stem: You are the events coordinator for your university's international student club. The club wants to hold a picnic in Greenfield Park next month to welcome new members, and you expect about forty people. The city's Parks Department website says that groups of more than twenty-five must reserve a picnic area, but it does not explain the rules about food, music or cost. You decide to email the Parks Department.
task: Write an email to the city's Parks Department. In your email, do the following:
bullets: Describe the event you are planning.
Ask about the rules for groups.
Give details of the dates you would prefer.
explanation:
Dear Parks Department,
I am the events coordinator for the International Student Club at the university. We are planning a welcome picnic for new members in Greenfield Park next month, and we expect about forty people to attend. Your website says that groups of more than twenty-five must reserve a picnic area, so I am writing to ask about the process.
Could you please tell me what rules apply to large groups? In particular, I would like to know whether we may bring our own food and a small portable grill, whether quiet music is allowed, and how much the reservation costs.
Our first choice would be Saturday the 14th, from 11 a.m. to 3 p.m. If that date is not available, Sunday the 15th or Saturday the 21st at the same time would also work for us.
Thank you for your help.
Best regards,
Sam
points: Introduces the writer's role and describes the event with useful numbers.
Asks clear, specific questions about the rules.
Gives a first choice and alternative dates with times.
Uses a polite, formal tone suitable for a city office.

stem: You are doing an internship in the research department of a software company. Your supervisor, Mr. Osei, asked you to collect and organize customer feedback for a new mobile app, and he expected the task to take three weeks. You finished it in two weeks. You enjoyed the work, and you have noticed that the design team is preparing user tests that you would like to learn about.
task: Write an email to your internship supervisor. In your email, do the following:
bullets: Tell him what you have finished.
Ask for a new task.
Suggest a project you would like to help with.
explanation:
Dear Mr. Osei,
I wanted to let you know that I have finished organizing the customer feedback for the new mobile app. I sorted more than three hundred comments into categories, such as speed, design and payment problems, and I added a one-page summary of the most common issues. The file is in our shared team folder.
Since I finished a week earlier than planned, I would be glad to take on a new task. I have really enjoyed working with the customer data, and I would like to keep learning as much as possible during my internship.
If it is possible, I would be very interested in helping the design team with their upcoming user tests. I could help to recruit participants, take notes during the sessions, or compare the results with the feedback I have already collected.
Thank you for your guidance.
Best regards,
Sam
points: Reports the completed work with specific, impressive details.
Asks for more work in a positive, professional way.
Suggests a relevant project and explains how the writer could contribute.
Uses a polite, confident tone suitable for a supervisor.

stem: Your university library lets students reserve group study rooms through an online booking system. Last Tuesday you reserved a room for your project group from 2 to 4 p.m. and received a confirmation. When your group arrived, another group was already using the room, and they also had a confirmation for the same time. The front desk could not find another free room, so your group had to work in a noisy café.
task: Write an email to the library's front desk staff. In your email, do the following:
bullets: Describe what happened last Tuesday.
Explain why this was a problem for your group.
Suggest a change to the booking system.
explanation:
Dear Library Staff,
I am writing about a problem with the study room booking system. Last Tuesday I reserved Room 2C from 2 to 4 p.m. for my project group and received a confirmation email. When we arrived, however, another group was already in the room, and they had a confirmation for exactly the same time.
The front desk staff were very helpful, but there were no other rooms available, so we had to work in a crowded café nearby. Because it was so noisy, we could not practice our presentation, which we have to give in class this Friday.
It seems that the system allowed two bookings for the same room. Would it be possible to add a check that stops this from happening? It might also help if the confirmation email included a code that students could show at the desk.
Thank you for looking into this.
Best regards,
Sam
points: Describes the double booking clearly with the room and time.
Explains the consequence for the group's work.
Offers a constructive, specific suggestion for the system.
Stays polite and even thanks the staff, rather than blaming them.

stem: You rent a house with two roommates. Last week the kitchen faucet started leaking, and now water drips constantly, even when the handle is turned off. This morning you noticed a dark stain on the cabinet under the sink, and the wood feels soft. Your landlord, Mrs. Thompson, lives in another town and usually prefers that tenants contact her by email. You are worried that the damage will get worse.
task: Write an email to your landlord, Mrs. Thompson. In your email, do the following:
bullets: Describe the problem in the kitchen.
Explain what you have done so far.
Ask her to arrange a repair and say when you are home.
explanation:
Dear Mrs. Thompson,
I am writing to let you know about a problem in the kitchen at 18 Willow Lane. Last week the kitchen faucet started leaking, and now it drips all the time, even when it is turned off completely. This morning I also found a dark stain on the cabinet under the sink, and the wood there feels soft.
To stop more damage, I have placed a bowl under the pipe and moved everything out of the cabinet so that it can dry. I also took photos of the faucet and the cabinet, which I have attached to this email.
Could you please arrange for a plumber to come as soon as possible? My roommates and I are usually at home in the mornings before 10 a.m., and someone will be there all day on Thursday.
Thank you very much.
Best regards,
Sam
points: Describes the leak and the damage precisely.
Shows responsible action already taken (the bowl, the photos).
Makes a clear request with specific availability for the repair.
Uses a polite, formal tone suitable for a landlord.

stem: Next month you will attend a three-day conference on renewable energy for students and young researchers. You registered online two weeks ago and paid the student fee of ninety dollars. Yesterday you checked your bank statement and saw that the fee had been charged twice. You also realized that you forgot to choose a workshop during registration. The conference has a contact email for its registration team.
task: Write an email to the conference registration team. In your email, do the following:
bullets: Explain the problem with your payment.
Ask them to fix the problem.
Ask a question about something else related to the conference.
explanation:
Dear Registration Team,
I registered online for the Renewable Energy Student Conference two weeks ago and paid the student fee of ninety dollars. Yesterday, however, I checked my bank statement and noticed that the fee was charged twice on the same day, so I have paid one hundred eighty dollars in total.
Could you please check my registration and refund the extra payment? My registration number is RE-2241, and I would be happy to send a copy of my bank statement if that would help.
I also have one more question. During registration I forgot to choose a workshop for the second day. Is it still possible to sign up for one? I am especially interested in the workshop on solar panel design, if there is still space.
Thank you for your help, and I look forward to the conference.
Best regards,
Sam
points: Explains the double charge with exact amounts.
Requests a refund and provides information to identify the registration.
Asks a separate, clear question about the workshop.
Uses a polite, formal tone and ends positively.

stem: Last weekend your friend Aisha lent you her bicycle so that you could ride to a job interview across town. On the way back, you rode over broken glass, and the front tire got a flat. You walked the bike home, and it is now in your building's storage room. Aisha needs the bike to get to her classes starting next Monday, and you want to make things right.
task: Write an email to your friend Aisha. In your email, do the following:
bullets: Tell her what happened to the bicycle.
Apologize and explain how you will fix the problem.
Suggest a time to return the bicycle.
explanation:
Hi Aisha,
Thanks again for lending me your bike on Saturday. The interview went really well! Unfortunately, on the way home I rode over some broken glass, and the front tire got a flat. I had to walk the rest of the way, so the bike is in my building's storage room right now.
I'm really sorry about this. I know you need the bike for classes next week, so I'm going to take it to the repair shop on Hill Street tomorrow and get a new tire and tube. Of course, I'll pay for everything.
The shop says it should be ready by Friday afternoon. Could I bring it over to your place on Friday at around 6 p.m.? If that doesn't work, I could drop it off on Saturday morning instead.
Thanks for understanding!
Best regards,
Sam
points: Explains what happened honestly and clearly.
Apologizes sincerely and takes responsibility with a concrete plan.
Suggests specific times to return the bike, with an alternative.
Uses a warm, informal tone with contractions, suitable for a friend.

stem: You joined your university's language exchange program, which matches students so they can practice each other's languages. You were matched with a partner named Chen, and the program asked you to meet once a week for one hour. Over the past month, Chen has canceled three of your four meetings at the last minute. You still want to practice Mandarin. The program is run by a coordinator, Ms. Patel.
task: Write an email to the program coordinator. In your email, do the following:
bullets: Describe the problem with your language exchange.
Explain what you hope to get from the program.
Suggest a solution.
explanation:
Dear Ms. Patel,
I am writing about my experience in the language exchange program this semester. I was matched with a partner named Chen, and we agreed to meet every Thursday afternoon. However, over the past month, three of our four meetings were canceled at the last minute.
I am sure Chen is very busy, and I do not want to cause any problems for him. Still, I joined the program because I want to improve my spoken Mandarin before a study abroad semester next year, and regular conversation practice is the most useful thing for me.
Would it be possible to be matched with a second partner, or with a different partner whose schedule fits better? I am free on Tuesday and Thursday afternoons and on Saturday mornings. Alternatively, a small group session could also work well.
Thank you for your help.
Best regards,
Sam
points: Describes the problem factually without criticizing the partner unfairly.
Explains the writer's goals, which makes the request reasonable.
Suggests specific solutions and gives availability.
Uses a polite, formal tone suitable for a program coordinator.

stem: You work part-time at a bookstore in the city center, and your shift on Saturday was supposed to start at 9 a.m. On the way to work, the bus you were on broke down, and you had to wait forty minutes for another one. Your phone battery was also dead, so you could not call the store. You arrived an hour late. Your manager, Ms. Hughes, was not at the store that day.
task: Write an email to your manager, Ms. Hughes. In your email, do the following:
bullets: Explain why you arrived late.
Apologize and describe what you did when you arrived.
Explain how you will avoid this problem in the future.
explanation:
Dear Ms. Hughes,
I am writing to explain why I arrived an hour late for my shift last Saturday. On the way to work, the bus I was on broke down, and I had to wait forty minutes for the next one. Unfortunately, my phone battery had also run out, so I could not call the store to let anyone know.
I am very sorry for the trouble this caused. As soon as I arrived, I apologized to Lucas, who had been working alone, and I stayed an extra hour after my shift to help unpack the new delivery.
In the future, I will take an earlier bus on weekend mornings so that I have more time if there is a delay. I will also carry a portable phone charger so that I can always contact the store.
Thank you for your understanding.
Best regards,
Sam
points: Explains the cause of the delay clearly and honestly.
Apologizes and shows responsibility through actions taken that day.
Describes specific steps to prevent the problem in the future.
Uses a respectful, professional tone suitable for an employer.
